description:
'''Complextro''' is typified by [[glitch (music)|glitchy]], intricate [[bassline]]s and textures created by sharply cutting between instruments in quick succession. The term, a [[portmanteau]] of the words "complex" and "electro", was coined by [[Porter Robinson]] to describe the music he was making in 2010. He has cited [[video game music|video game sounds]], or [[chiptune]]s, as an influence on his music, along with 1980s [[analog synthesizer|analog synth]] music.

While Robinson was the first to give the subgenre a name, he was not the creator of the general sound. No one musician can be solely considered the genre's progenitor, but its earliest origins can likely be attributed to [[Justice (band)|Justice]], who combined the [[French house]] style popularized by [[Daft Punk]] with the faster and more aggressive sounds emerging in electronic music in [[Europe]]. Songs like their 2005 [[Waters of Nazareth]] typify the sounds that would later become popular in complextro.

Like the sonically similar [[Dubstep#2011:_Brostep_and_American_developments|brostep]] subgenre, a precise definition of "complextro" is difficult to state, because of its initial popularity on the Internet (rather than in clubs) and several other factors. Notably, complextro gained popularity on YouTube gaming channels and was also used in commercials, exposing the genre to a broader audience that didn't otherwise listen to as much electronic music. Additionally, the term was often derided or used disparagingly on forums by fans of electro house or other electronic music who didn't like the new genre's sound or its fanbase. Further complicating the usage of the term was the fact that many artists who made "brostep" also produced complextro or sonically similar music, often using the same sound design techniques in both genres. A good example of this is [[Skrillex]]'s [[Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites]] [[EP]], which featured two complextro songs ([[Rock 'n' Roll (Will Take You to the Mountain)|Rock 'n' Roll]] and Kill Everybody) and two "brostep" songs ([[Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites|Scary Monsters]] and Scatta).

Other popular producers of the genre include [[Cash Cash]], [[Adventure Club]], [[Kill the Noise]], [[Jon Gooch|Feed Me]], [[Knife Party]], [[The M Machine]], [[Madeon]], [[Mord Fustang]], [[Savant (musician)|Savant]], [[Virtual Riot]], [[Wolfgang Gartner]].
